item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 071721
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Wed Oct 7 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, and on newly formed Tropical
Depression 20-E, located several hundred miles south-southeast of
Lazaro Cardenas, Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala during the early portion of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for some gradual development of this
system thereafter while it moves generally west-northwestward at
around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression 20-E are issued under WMO
header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression 20-E are issued under WMO
header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Pasch

...RACHEL MOVES WEST-NORTHWESTWARD OVER THE EASTERN PACIFIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.9N 121.8W
ABOUT 775 MI...1245 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 20.9 North, longitude 121.8 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h), and a generally west
to west-northwestward motion is expected during the next couple of
days. Rachel is then forecast to slow down before making a sharp
turn to the northeast by the end of the week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 80 mph (130 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual to steady weakening is forecast over the next few
days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Berg

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 42
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Wed Oct 07 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 071452
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  42
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM PDT Wed Oct 07 2026
 
Recent satellite imagery shows that Rachel's deep convection has
waned over the last couple of hours, however this could be due to
the convective daily minimum. If this is the case, then there is a 
good chance for deep convection to return later. The northern side 
of the cyclone still shows the impact of easterly shear and dry air
intrusions.  The eye of the hurricane is still well defined based
on the proxy-visible satellite imagery. Looking at a combination of
the objective and subjective intensity estimates, the initial
intensity for this advisory is being held at 70 kt.
 
The initial motion for the cyclone is west-northwestward, or 285/6
kt. As of now, Rachel is being steered by high pressure located
over the western United States. However, toward the end of the
week, a large mid- to upper-level trough is expected to approach
from the northwest. This will cause Rachel to slow down and
then turn and accelerate toward Baja California and southern 
California, and the updated NHC forecast track shows Rachel as 
a post-tropical cyclone at 96 h very near the coast. The current NHC 
forecast provides a 120-h track point for forecast continuity, 
however it is likely that the cyclone could dissipate sooner once it 
moves over land. The rest of the forecast is similar to the previous 
track with minor adjustments made based on the latest HCCA and GDMI
forecast aids, except for the track point at 120 h.
 
The hurricane is expected to gradually weaken as it moves into an
unfavorable environment of cooler sea-surface temperatures and
limited moisture. Given how resilient Rachel has been to the
environment, the current intensity trend is on the upper end of the
guidance envelope. There is still a higher-than-normal amount of
uncertainty to the intensity for the latter portion of the forecast.
The trough should induce plenty of wind shear, and the simulated
satellite guidance does show that the cyclone loses convection for a
brief time before it comes back again. The current NHC forecast does
show a post-tropical cyclone at 96 h, however, it is possible that
it could still have tropical-storm-force winds at that point. In
general, the current NHC intensity forecast is very similar to the
previous one with a few changes past 60 h, based on the HCCA and
GDMI forecast aids.

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Public Advisory Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Wed Oct 07 2026 
736 
WTPZ35 KNHC 072039
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Simon Advisory Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Wed Oct 07 2026
 
...DEPRESSION BECOMES TROPICAL STORM SIMON...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.5N 101.6W
ABOUT 175 MI...285 KM SSE OF LAZARO CARDENAS MEXICO
ABOUT 300 MI...485 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of this system.  Watches will likely be required for a
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico tonight.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was
located near latitude 15.5 North, longitude 101.6 West.  Simon is
moving toward the west-northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected to continue through tomorrow, followed 
by a turn toward the northwest and north on Friday.  On the 
forecast track, the center of Simon is expected to remain south of 
Mexico through Friday, but approach the coast of southwestern Mexico 
on Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Continued strengthening is forecast during 
the next 48 hours, and Simon is expected to become a hurricane 
by late Thursday.  It could become a major hurricane by Saturday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone 
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.

RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 12
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals between 15 and 25 inches possible across portions of Colima
and Michoacan through Sunday.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Wed Oct 07 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 072039
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Wed Oct 07 2026

The system continues to gradually become better organized on 
satellite imagery with convective banding features becoming more 
prominent.  The latest subjective Dvorak classification from TAFB 
had a T-number of 2.5, corresponding to an intensity of 35 kt.  On 
this basis, the cyclone is being upgraded to Tropical Storm Simon 
for this advisory.  The storm has developed upper-level anticyclonic 
outflow over all quadrants of the circulation.

ASCAT-B scatterometer data suggested that the center of the cyclone 
is a little north of the previous track, but the overall motion 
still appears to be toward the west-northwest, or about 300/7 kt.  
Simon is likely to continue this general west-northwestward motion 
for the next day or so, to the south of a weak mid-level ridge.  By 
Friday, the system should turn northwestward and then northward 
ahead of a 500 mb trough approaching Baja California. In 3-5 days, 
the cyclone should move generally northward between a mid-level 
anticyclone and the trough near Baja California.  The official 
forecast track remains on the right side of the guidance envelope, 
and is close to the Google DeepMind ensemble mean.
 
For the next few days, Simon is expected to remain within an 
environment of low vertical wind shear and moist low- to mid-level 
air, while moving over waters of high oceanic heat content.  These 
factors should result in a significant increase in intensity this 
week, and the system is likely to strengthen into a hurricane, 
and then into a major hurricane later this week.  The NHC intensity 
forecast is a little above the intensity model consensus, IVCN.

Key Messages:

1. Simon is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by Thursday 
night and approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major 
hurricane on Saturday. 

2. There is a risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts along 
portions of the west-central coast of Mexico over the weekend and 
into early next week, and watches could be required by tonight.

3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern Mexico later this week and into the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain.

4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central 
coast of Mexico through the weekend.  These swells are likely to 
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please 
consult products from your local weather office.
